items.label: Who to target first
items.evidence: Goal: cut while keeping strength, recomp, lean bulk, or break a plateau
items.reason: Names cutting lifters who want to keep strength, but only as one of several goals and never mentions GLP-1 users or weight loss as the lead.

items.label: Second segment worth a test
items.reason: Never names midlife men, home-gym lifters, or time-constrained older adults as a segment.

items.label: Verdict on the founder's starting guess
items.evidence: your customer guess is directionally right, but too broad
items.reason: Calls the guess too broad but keeps dual-tracking lifters as the lead rather than shifting to weight-loss or GLP-1 users.

items.label: What to say
items.evidence: Lead with integrated insight, not consolidation
items.reason: Leads with the combined-log/AI-insight message; muscle preservation appears only as one goal among several.

items.label: The pain and the moment people buy
items.evidence: a cut where strength is dropping
items.reason: Names strength loss during a cut and plateau as the trigger, but never covers low protein or suppressed appetite.

items.label: Top objections to handle
items.reason: Handles only the trust-in-AI objection; no medical/safety, privacy, or price-versus-alternatives objection.

items.label: What they use today
items.evidence: Currently uses two apps—a macro/calorie app plus a strength/workout app
items.reason: Describes the two-app split clearly but names no actual competitor or AI/coaching alternative they use today.

items.label: Claims to avoid
items.evidence: People needing medical nutrition advice—different trust/regulatory burden
items.reason: Alludes to regulatory burden in general terms without saying which claims to avoid.

items.label: Where to reach them
items.evidence: Recruit from Reddit fitness communities, Discord servers, Instagram/TikTok lifters
items.reason: Names community and creator channels but no comparison/search pages or YouTube demos, and Reddit is generic fitness rather than lifting or GLP-1.
